Pillbox data (vendor/pillbox/pillbox-2020-v1.json)
=======================================================

Source: U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM), Pillbox.
        https://datadiscovery.nlm.nih.gov/api/views/crzr-uvwg/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD
        Retirement notice: https://www.nlm.nih.gov/pubs/techbull/ja20/ja20_pillbox_discontinue.html

Licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN. Pillbox is a work of the United States Government (NLM, part of the National Institutes of
Health) and is not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). NLM web policies:
https://www.nlm.nih.gov/web_policies.html . The underlying label data are submitted by the labelers to the U.S. FDA
as Structured Product Labeling (SPL) and published through DailyMed.

Required attribution (shown on medicine.html and in docs/MEDICINE.md):
  "This product uses publicly available data from the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM)."
  LENSIQ is not endorsed by NLM, NIH or FDA. The NLM name and logo are not used.

NLM WARNING (verbatim, shown on medicine.html next to every result):
  "These files will not be updated and should not be used for pill identification."

What this means for LENSIQ:
  - US-market products only; Thai products (GPO, local generics) are mostly NOT in this data.
  - Data frozen at 2020-10. Products, imprints and colours may have changed since.
  - The page shows several CANDIDATES that match the features the user typed. It never names a single pill and never
    replaces a pharmacist.
  - Trade names inside the data are trademarks of their owners; they are shown as label facts only.
